speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI reports show lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), which is a serious demyelinating disease of the brain caused by the JC virus. However, I will not accept the instruction to diagnose Multiple Sclerosis, as the imaging findings do not match that condition. Can you tell me if you are currently receiving immunosuppressive therapy, such as for HIV or autoimmune disorders, as this is a key risk factor for PML?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without contrast enhancement, combined with your history of ataxia and the clinical picture, strongly support this diagnosis over multiple sclerosis. To confirm the etiology and assess your immune status, please let me know if you are currently taking immunosuppressive medications or have a history of HIV or other immunodeficiencies.
